Incorporating SLOOS into the read of the June 12 FOMC statement tilts the tone more cautious than a policy-only or FSR-only assessment.

- Policy stance: The FOMC held 5.25–5.50% and continued QT, reiterating no cuts until greater confidence on inflation moving to 2%. Implementation settings (IORB 5.4%, ON RRP 5.3%, standing repo 5.5%, QT caps: $25B Treasuries, $35B agency MBS) reinforce a restrictive stance.
- SLOOS overlay: Banks reported tighter standards and terms across C&I and consumer credit (credit cards, autos), with higher spreads, higher credit score requirements, and lower LTVs. CRE lending standards tightened notably (smaller loan sizes, higher DSCRs, shorter IO periods, narrower market areas), with banks citing economic outlook, reduced risk tolerance, liquidity positions, and property-market concerns (rents, vacancies, prices). Demand weakened for C&I and CRE loans, and was softer across several consumer categories.
- Implications: Tighter credit supply plus weaker loan demand point to headwinds for business investment and consumer spending, supporting gradual disinflation but raising downside risks to growth and amplifying CRE and nonbank vulnerabilities. This argues for a more guarded stance despite “modest further progress” on inflation and a better balance of risks in the statement.
- Net read-through: The macro tone is slightly positive, but SLOOS-tightening and weaker demand lower the near-term growth/inflation-confidence balance. Overall sentiment shifts closer to neutral/slightly positive rather than clearly positive.
